ozet: Growing up with his uncle Abu Talib, tending sheep, and the journey to Syria with his uncle at the age of twelve.

b06-s01: When his grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib died, the Prophet was eight years old. Now his uncle Abu Talib would take him in, raise him and protect him.
From then on the Prophet grew up beside his uncle, together with him.
b06-s02: Abu Talib was a respected man whose word carried weight among Quraysh.
b06-s03: Abu Talib loved his nephew dearly.
He believed he brought good fortune, watched over him closely, and did all he could for him to be well brought up.
Abu Talib's wife, Fatima bint Asad, also cared for him even more than for her own children.
b06-s04: When the Prophet was about ten years old, he tended sheep to help his uncle, who had a large family.
b06-s05: Years later, after he became a prophet, he said one day: «Every prophet Allah sent tended sheep.»
When those with him asked, «And you?», he said: «Yes, I too tended the sheep of the people of Mecca for a small wage.»
b06-s06: Abu Talib kept his nephew with him even on his journeys.
When the Prophet was twelve years old, Abu Talib decided to go with a Quraysh caravan to trade in the land of Sham, that is, Syria.
b06-s07: When the time came to set out, according to the reports, the Prophet did not want to be parted from his uncle.
Abu Talib's heart softened and he said: «By Allah, I will take him with me. He and I will never be parted.»
b06-s08: The caravan travelled north towards the lands of Syria and halted at Busra.
Busra was a market town to the south of Damascus; the caravans of Quraysh often stopped there.
b06-s09: According to a report told in the sources of the Prophet's life, there was a monk named Bahira who lived in his monastery at Busra.
Bahira had never paid any attention to the Quraysh caravans that passed by before, nor spoken with anyone.
But this time he saw a cloud shading the Prophet in the caravan, and the branches of the tree he sat under bending over him.
b06-s10: At once he had a meal prepared and invited the whole company.
Because the Prophet was young, he had been left beside the baggage. Bahira asked that he come too.
b06-s11: Bahira wanted to ask him some questions in the name of al-Lat and al-'Uzza, the idols Quraysh swore by.
The Prophet replied: «Do not ask me in the name of al-Lat and al-'Uzza. By Allah, there is nothing I hate more than them.»

So Bahira asked in the name of Allah; he asked about his state in sleep, his appearance and his affairs. His answers matched the description Bahira knew. Then he looked at his back and saw the seal of prophethood there.
b06-s12: Then he turned to Abu Talib and told him to take his nephew back home and to protect him from the Jews.
«This nephew of yours will have a great future», he said.
Abu Talib quickly finished his business in Syria and returned to Mecca with his nephew.
b06-s13: The soundness of the report of this meeting is disputed; some scholars did not find it authentic and rejected it, while others accepted it as true.
The Prophet, meanwhile, went on growing up under Allah's protection, far from the evils of the Age of Ignorance.
